articles.title: France: Riot police clash with school protesters and use tear gas
articles.summary: Hundreds of thousands of people have taken to the streets across France amid a wave of protests by high-school pupils.
articles.body:
Hundreds of thousands of people have taken to the streets across France, as a wave of protests by high-school pupils spread to their parents, university students and unions.

Crowds of teenagers marched from the Place de la République in Paris, calling for more resources for schools, and what they called less repression from police.

Police clashed with demonstrators in Lyon, used tear gas in Paris and Marseille and water cannon in Rennes, but there was little of the serious trouble that marred previous protests.

articles.title: Garba’s new luxury flex: Valet, VVIP seats and butlers
articles.summary: Luxury garba packages debut in Vadodara and Ahmedabad this Navratri, offering valet parking, VVIP seats, butlers and more, priced Rs10,620–2.75 lakh.
articles.body: VADODARA/AHMEDABAD: Forget crowded grounds, chaotic parking, long queues at food counters and the frantic hunt for a decent seat. This Navratri, traditional garba is getting a luxury makeover, with organisers offering revellers everything from valet parking and VVIP seating to butler service, personal photographers and even foot massages — at a premium ranging from Rs 14,000 a night to Rs 1.21 lakh for a VIP table.Several major garba organisers in Vadodara have rolled out premium packages for those seeking the traditional experience without the usual festival scramble. Depending on the package, guests can get special entry, reserved parking, food, VVIP seating and even access to aarti.At Laxmi Vilas Palace Heritage Garba, the premium package costs around Rs 10,620 per night on regular days and Rs 14,750 on weekends and the eighth night. It includes a player’s pass, aarti access, VVIP seating, special entry, reserved parking, food vouchers and a guest relationship executive.The organisers say the package has found takers particularly among visitors from outside Vadodara. “The premium package is useful for people coming from outside who may not know their way around the venue. Many come for just a day or two to experience traditional Garba. It is similar to the premium experience offered at large music events,” said Prachi Shah, member of the advisory committee of LVP Heritage Garba, organised by the royal Gaekwad family’s trust.Kanku Pagla, hosting garba for two nights, has gone a step further. Its premium offering includes valet parking, quick entry and specially designed photo spots. A VIP table for up to 10 people costs Rs 1.21 lakh and comes with player passes, butler service, a dedicated photographer and food. “These services are particularly popular with people coming from outside Gujarat and NRIs. The players and audiences want to enjoy garba without chaos and we are offering it,” said Nitin Nanavaty, one of the organisers of Kanku Pagla.Vadodara Vibrant Navratri (VVN), meanwhile, has introduced combo packages. Its Rs 25,000 elite package includes seats in the elite tower, food, VIP parking and four unisex player passes. A corporate package offers 15 player passes, audience passes and two VIP parking slots. “We also offer direct access to the food arena and special facilities to all the players,” a VVN spokesperson said.Ahmedabad’s luxury garba circuit is taking the premium experience further, with one event charging up to Rs 27,500 per person for an exclusive Gazebo package.Safed Parindey, billed as an ultra-luxurious garba experience, has priced regular passes at Rs 15,000 per person. Its top-end Rs 2.75 lakh Gazebo for 10 people works out to Rs 27,500 per person and includes home pick-up and drop, personal security, private dining with coffee, in-Gazebo foot massages and a goodie bag.The event follows an all-white luxury theme, with the Ahmedabad venue yet to be revealed. articles.title: Brasileiro preso por usar fantasia do ICE pagou fiança de R$ 29,5 mil | G1
articles.standfirst: Danilo Silva foi detido após se passar por agente imigratório para intimidar eleitores em ponto de votação das eleições brasileiras.
articles.summary: Danilo Silva foi detido após se passar por agente imigratório para intimidar eleitores em ponto de votação das eleições brasileiras.
articles.body:
O brasileiro Danilo Silva , detido no último domingo (5) por se fantasiar de agente do ICE para intimidar eleitores em um local de votação, teve de pagar US$ 5.650 (R$ 29.506) de fiança para não ser preso .

Durante a audiência de custódia, a juíza Mindy Glazer , do 11º circuito judicial da Flórida, o repreendeu. “Isso não é Halloween”, ela disse, em referência à celebração do dia das bruxas no país. "Halloween é no dia 31", afirmou.

Ele foi acusado de intimidação eleitoral qualificada, suborno, ameaça a agentes públicos, uso ilegal de insígnias policiais e conduta desordeira. Silva foi solto após pagar a fiança determinada pela Justiça.

Agora, ele deve prestar novo depoimento em 19 de outubro. O caso seguirá para análise da Promotoria, que decidirá se apresenta formalmente as acusações contra ele, segundo a "ABC News".

A prisão ocorreu durante o primeiro dia de votação das eleições presidenciais brasileiras no exterior. As autoridades afirmam que brasileiro usava um uniforme semelhante ao dos agentes de imigração dos EUA e circulava entre os eleitores para provocar temor.

Segundo a polícia, após ser abordado, ele admitiu que não era agente federal e disse que o traje havia sido comprado pela internet. De acordo com o relatório policial, ele se exaltou durante a abordagem, ameaçou um investigador e chegou a oferecer dinheiro aos agentes para evitar a prisão.

Aos investigadores, ele afirmou que queria apenas observar a reação das pessoas.

Danilo Silva alegou às autoridades que só usou a fantasia para "ver a reação das pessoas". — Foto: Foto: Administração penitenciária do condado de Miami-Dade.

articles.title: Alunos e professores protestam na França no maior dia de mobilização | G1
articles.standfirst: Manifestações desta terça ocorrem após duas semanas de protestos que começaram nos subúrbios carentes de Paris antes de se espalharem por todo o país. Pelo menos 256 mil pessoas foram para as ruas.
articles.summary: Manifestações desta terça ocorrem após duas semanas de protestos que se espalharam por todo o país. Pelo menos 256 mil pessoas foram para as ruas.
articles.body:
Alunos, professores e pais marcharam em cidades por toda a França nesta terça-feira, e manifestantes bloquearam centenas de escolas, no maior dia de mobilização de uma onda de manifestações que exigem que o governo resolva o problema da falta de pessoal e das salas de aula em mau estado.

Em Marselha, Nantes e Lyon, os protestos de rua começaram pacificamente no meio da manhã, com a maior manifestação prevista para Paris à tarde.

Os jovens erguiam sinalizadores de fumaça e cartazes com frases como “Sob nossos livros escolares, raiva” e “Onde estão os políticos? Será que eles sabem que existimos?”

Manifestantes exibem cartazes e bandeiras durante uma manifestação de estudantes do ensino médio e universitário, apoiados pelo sindicato dos professores e pais de alunos, em Paris. — Foto: Abdul Saboor/Reuters

As manifestações desta terça-feira ocorrem após duas semanas de protestos que começaram nos subúrbios carentes de Paris antes de se espalharem por todo o país. O governo respondeu com a polícia de choque, afirmando que o movimento havia se transformado em violência urbana.

A mão de um adolescente foi arrancada durante confrontos entre manifestantes do ensino médio e a polícia de choque no norte da França na segunda-feira. François-Xavier Lauch, prefeito de Pas-de-Calais, se recusou a comentar as circunstâncias exatas, afirmando que cerca de 200 a 250 manifestantes estavam atirando objetos contra a polícia.

O jornal regional La Voix du Nord informou que o adolescente de 15 anos perdeu a mão e parte do antebraço após pegar uma granada de dispersão da polícia.

A União dos Estudantes do Ensino Médio informou que 1.800 escolas do ensino médio estavam bloqueadas ou fechariam durante o dia. Algumas autoridades educacionais locais tentaram transferir as aulas para o ambiente virtual. O Ministério da Educação não divulgou os números imediatamente.

“Quando a resposta é a violência, isso significa que a democracia não está mais funcionando”, disse Hugo Vetzel, um recém-formado do ensino médio em Estrasburgo que agora está fazendo cursos preparatórios para os exames de admissão nas melhores universidades da França . “Existe uma enorme distância entre as elites e nós.”

Um manifestante mascarado atira um objeto em meio a confrontos com a polícia francesa durante uma manifestação de estudantes do ensino médio e universitário. — Foto: Yves Herman/Reuters

O primeiro-ministro Sébastien Lecornu ordenou que seus ministros atendam às principais reivindicações dos estudantes . Entre elas estão garantir a substituição de professores ausentes, rever a duração do dia letivo, das 8h às 18h, e a necessidade de intervalos de almoço mais longos.

O governo também analisará os reparos necessários nos prédios escolares antigos, disse Lecornu, que exigiu que os ministros enviassem suas primeiras propostas até o final de outubro.

O Ministério do Interior da França informou que 6.100 pessoas foram presas desde o início dos protestos, sendo a esmagadora maioria delas menores de idade. Mais de 1.800 pessoas estão sendo processadas, incluindo 1.483 menores, informou o Ministério da Justiça, sem especificar os crimes.

Pelo menos 715 policiais e 215 adolescentes ficaram feridos nos confrontos, segundo o gabinete de Lecornu.

articles.title: Bombeiros treinam resgate a 100 metros de altura em curso inédito | G1
articles.standfirst: Sete militares participam da capacitação, que tem 200 horas e inclui simulações de resgates a até 100 metros de altura.
articles.summary: Sete militares participam da capacitação, que tem 200 horas e inclui simulações de resgates a até 100 metros de altura.
articles.body:
Pela primeira vez, Mato Grosso do Sul realiza um curso de especialização para formar bombeiros preparados para resgates em grandes alturas. Sete militares participam da capacitação, que inclui simulações a até 100 metros do chão e em diferentes ambientes de risco, como a torre da TV Morena e prédios de Campo Grande .

Com 200 horas de duração, o curso reproduz situações de alta complexidade para ensinar técnicas de acesso, imobilização e retirada de vítimas em locais elevados, sempre com foco na segurança dos bombeiros e dos socorridos.

A proposta é reproduzir situações semelhantes às encontradas pelos bombeiros durante ocorrências reais, preparando os militares para realizar resgates com segurança tanto para a vítima quanto para a própria equipe.

O soldado Gustavo Maximo, que está há dois anos na corporação, é um dos alunos da turma e afirma que o trabalho exige mais do que força física.

“Realmente precisa ter muita técnica, muito conhecimento. Não adianta achar que vai fazer força e vai conseguir se não tiver o conhecimento técnico, a expertise de saber na hora certa. É muito difícil trabalhar, então esse curso permite atuar de forma melhor e poder salvar vítimas”, afirma.

Segundo o major Evaldo Nunes de Oliveira, coordenador do curso, os militares começam com técnicas de progressão em corda, ascensão e movimentação lateral. Ao longo da capacitação, o nível de dificuldade aumenta gradualmente.

Bombeiros fazem treinamento inédito em MS — Foto: CBMMS

Os alunos também treinam diferentes tipos de salvamento, desde ocorrências envolvendo vítimas sem lesões até situações em que é necessário realizar imobilização e movimentações mais complexas, com utilização de mais equipamentos.

“Eles começam com progressão em corda, ascensão, movimentação lateral e várias situações. Depois, continuamos com as atividades de salvamento, intensificando a complexidade das ocorrências”, explica o major.

A capacitação busca desenvolver não apenas a técnica de acesso à vítima, mas também os procedimentos necessários para garantir a segurança durante toda a operação.

Esta é a primeira vez que Mato Grosso do Sul realiza o curso de especialização em salvamento em altura.

Até o ano passado, os militares que precisavam dessa capacitação tinham que viajar para outros estados, como São Paulo, Paraná e Distrito Federal.

Com o credenciamento do curso em Mato Grosso do Sul, a expectativa do Corpo de Bombeiros é ampliar a quantidade de turmas e, consequentemente, aumentar o número de militares capacitados para atuar nesse tipo de ocorrência.

Doze militares já concluíram a capacitação e, nesta edição, atuam como instrutores da nova turma.

Entre eles está a soldado Polyana Wruck, que fez o treinamento em São Paulo. Ela é a única mulher da corporação em Mato Grosso do Sul com o diploma do curso e agora participa da formação dos novos especialistas.

Para a instrutora, a segurança dos bombeiros é uma das premissas do trabalho de salvamento em altura.

“Uma das premissas do resgate é nós, bombeiros, estarmos em segurança e oferecer essa segurança também para a nossa vítima. As técnicas que aprendemos durante o curso são fundamentais para que a gente atenda à ocorrência e faça o resgate totalmente em segurança”, afirma.

articles.title: Univás reabre curso de Pedagogia unindo tradição e inovação | G1
articles.standfirst: A Universidade do Vale do Sapucaí (Univás), em Pouso Alegre, reabre o curso de Pedagogia com uma matriz curricular totalmente reformulada para os ingressantes em 2027
articles.summary: A Universidade do Vale do Sapucaí (Univás), em Pouso Alegre, reabre o curso de Pedagogia com uma matriz curricular totalmente reformulada para os ingressantes em 2027
articles.body:
Univás reabre curso de Pedagogia unindo tradição e inovação — Foto: Crédito: Divulgação

A Universidade do Vale do Sapucaí (Univás), em Pouso Alegre, está reabrindo o curso de Pedagogia com uma matriz curricular totalmente reformulada para os ingressantes em 2027. Com duração de quatro anos, a formação tem como proposta articular conhecimentos sobre educação, formação para a docência, pesquisa, estágio e extensão ao longo da graduação.

“Decidimos ofertar esse curso que é de licenciatura no período noturno. Lembrando, que essa renovação se insere na trajetória de um curso criado em 1972 na nossa universidade, conectando sua experiência na formação de educadores às demandas contemporâneas da educação. Portanto, nosso curso de Pedagogia combina tradição acadêmica, inovação curricular, pesquisa desde o primeiro semestre e experiências práticas em contextos reais. Na Univás, a formação para a docência se articula à gestão e coordenação pedagógica, à pesquisa e à atuação em diferentes espaços educativos”, observa o reitor da Univás, José Dias da Silva Neto.

Segundo a coordenadora do curso de Pedagogia da Univás, Letícia Rodrigues de Souza, a nova proposta prepara o futuro pedagogo para compreender diferentes formas de aprender, planejar situações de ensino, acompanhar o desenvolvimento dos estudantes e construir práticas que favoreçam sua participação.

“Esse compromisso aparece em conteúdos sobre alfabetização, educação inclusiva, direitos humanos, diversidade, tecnologias e gestão educacional. O enfoque é formar profissionais capazes de analisar situações do cotidiano educativo e tomar decisões pedagógicas fundamentadas”, acrescenta.

As inscrições para o curso de Pedagogia da Univás podem ser feitas em duas modalidades a critério do candidato. Na Modalidade I, as inscrições são feitas exclusivamente via Internet. Neste caso, a prova on-line será liberada em até dois dias úteis, após o pagamento da taxa de inscrição. Na Modalidade II, as inscrições são feitas exclusivamente via internet. Neste caso, os inscritos devem informar o número da inscrição e ano do Enem para verificação de sua pontuação.

Lembrando, que o curso de Pedagogia da Univás vai contar com 20 Bolsas de Estudos de Assistência Social, com cobertura de 50% do valor das mensalidades. A concessão das bolsas seguirá os critérios regulamentares estabelecidos pela Universidade.

Quatro anos de graduação com experiências práticas desde o ingresso

A matriz do curso de Pedagogia da Univás prevê 400 horas de estágio supervisionado e 320 horas de extensão, distribuídas pelos oito semestres.

“Também contempla 64 horas de Laboratório de Produção de Materiais Didáticos, integradas à formação. Queremos aproximar os estudos das experiências educativas”, ressalta Letícia.

No primeiro período, o componente Estágio Supervisionado I: Inserção na Escola prevê observação de espaços, rotinas, relações e documentos institucionais. Ao longo do percurso, os estágios contemplam experiências em Educação Infantil, alfabetização e anos iniciais, gestão, coordenação pedagógica e Educação de Jovens e Adultos. A aproximação com o trabalho profissional acontece de maneira progressiva e supervisionada.

Extensão vinculada às escolas e às comunidades

Conforme a coordenadora, os projetos integradores de extensão permitem trabalhar com demandas dos territórios, envolvendo escuta, planejamento, desenvolvimento e avaliação de ações educativas. Entre os temas previstos estão “Escola e Território”, “Inclusão e Participação” e “Alfabetização e Cultura”.

“Nosso curso de Pedagogia analisa e reconhece necessidades de uma comunidade. Dessa forma, queremos desenvolver ações de incentivo à leitura e produzir recursos acessíveis em diálogo com os participantes”, esclarece Letícia.

Pesquisa como parte da identidade profissional do professor

A formação para a pesquisa começa no primeiro semestre do curso de Pedagogia, com Introdução à Pesquisa na Universidade, e se aprofunda em componentes como Metodologia do Trabalho Científico e Pesquisa em Educação: Projeto e Métodos.

“Esse percurso desenvolve conhecimentos para selecionar fontes confiáveis, formular perguntas, investigar situações educacionais e elaborar propostas fundamentadas. A pesquisa é fundamental para capacitar o professor para compreender sua realidade de trabalho e aperfeiçoar suas práticas”, analisa a coordenadora.

Possibilidades de atuação e contribuição para a região

A formação do curso de Pedagogia contempla a docência na Educação Infantil e nos anos iniciais do Ensino Fundamental, além de conhecimentos relacionados à gestão e à coordenação pedagógica. “Também aborda o trabalho educativo em instituições culturais, sociais, comunitárias e organizacionais. O enfoque regional pode destacar a contribuição da proposta para a formação de educadores que conheçam os contextos em que atuam e desenvolvam ações em diálogo com escolas, famílias e comunidades. Essa relação está prevista nos componentes de estágio e extensão desde o início da graduação”, conta Letícia.

articles.title: Milhares protestam em apoio à ex-aluna que acusou 7 de estupro nos EUA | G1
articles.standfirst: Manifestação apoia ex-colega de faculdade que acusou sete homens de cometer um estupro coletivo em uma festa. O caso comoveu os EUA e também provocou críticas à própria instituição.
articles.summary: Manifestação apoia ex-colega de faculdade que acusou sete homens de cometer um estupro coletivo em uma festa. O caso comoveu os EUA e também provocou críticas à própria instituição
articles.body:
"Vergonha! Vergonha! Vergonha!" , era o que se ouvia na Universidade de Cornell durante uma manifestação em apoio a Jane Doe — nome usado nos autos judiciais para se referir à ex-aluna que acusa sete homens de estupro coletivo .

No início de outubro, milhares de estudantes se reuniram no campus da universidade em Ithaca, em Nova York, onde fica a sede da instituição.

Segundo relatos publicados pelo jornal estudantil The Cornell Daily Sun, Doe entrou com uma ação judicial afirmando que havia sido drogada e violentada coletivamente em uma festa na residência da fraternidade Chi Phi .

O caso provocou uma manifestação que, além de defender a ex-aluna, também cobra medidas da própria Universidade de Cornell . Os estudantes pedem a responsabilização dos supostos autores do crime e mudanças na administração da instituição.

Durante o protesto, estudantes também afirmaram não se sentir seguros no campus e criticaram a maneira como a universidade teria lidado com o caso.

A casa da fraternidade Chi Phi na Universidade Cornell em Ithaca, Nova York — Foto: AP/Heather Ainsworth

Uma das principais reivindicações dos estudantes é a renúncia do reitor da Universidade de Cornell, Michael Kotlikoff. A multidão também pede a expulsão dos supostos autores do crime ou a revogação de seus diplomas.

Os manifestantes exigem ainda uma i nvestigação externa sobre a administração da universidade . Segundo eles, é necessário garantir responsabilização, transparência e justiça não apenas para Jane Doe, mas também para outras possíveis sobreviventes.

"Eu não me sinto em segurança neste campus de jeito nenhum", afirmou Andrea Cicirello, estudante da Cornell, durante a manifestação. Em entrevista à DW, ele também criticou o que chamou de "cultura do estupro" na instituição.

Manifestante segura cartaz que diz "Cornell persegue manifestantes e protege estupradores". — Foto: Lauren Petracca/Reuters

Kaori Quan, outra estudante da universidade, afirmou ter a mesma preocupação. "Eu também não me sinto segura neste campus. Já chega. Os administradores deste campus não se importam com os estudantes. Demonstraram isso repetidas vezes" , disse.

Os estudantes também fizeram comparações com as punições aplicadas a manifestantes pró-Palestina. Segundo os participantes do protesto, houve falta de responsabilização no caso envolvendo Doe, enquanto manifestações pró-Palestina resultaram em suspensões consideradas severas por eles.

Comunidade escolar se junta à manifestação

Manifestantes seguram cartazes durante um protesto por Justiça para as Sobreviventes na Universidade Cornell em Ithaca, Nova York, EUA, em 5 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: Lauren Petracca/Reuters

Além dos estudantes, membros do corpo docente e moradores de Ithaca, cidade onde fica a universidade, participaram do protesto.

Entre eles estava Willa Urbanczyl, moradora da cidade, que criticou o que considera uma punição branda para parte dos estudantes apontados no processo.

"Eu acho realmente preocupante que, pelo que sei, cinco dos estudantes envolvidos nesse incidente pudessem simplesmente continuar seus estudos, basicamente, com uma pena leve", afirmou. "Então, sim, eu esperava que eles ficassem na prisão pelo resto da vida."

A manifestação reuniu milhares de pessoas e colocou no centro do debate as cobranças dos estudantes por segurança, transparência e responsabilização dentro da Universidade de Cornell.

articles.title: In 2015, Washington bonded ultra-hard bauxite chips to a Snohomish County ramp with polymer resin; wet-weather crashes dropped from nearly 14 to one
articles.summary: Discover how Washington State's innovative application of high-friction bauxite surface treatment drastically reduced wet-weather crashes at a busy ramp by 93%, enhancing road safety and proving effective for state agencies nationwide.
articles.body: Roads rarely become dangerous without a reason. Ramps that curve onto busy highways are often where a vehicle is pushed beyond what its tyres can grip, because of a tight curve, a downhill approach and a layer of rain. Engineers call the grip between tyre and road friction. Drivers who have done nothing wrong can still slide out of their lane when friction is too low.Over the past ten years, one remedy has spread across the country: the high-friction surface treatment, which the Federal Highway Administration describes as a polish-resistant material such as calcined bauxite bonded to the road with a polymer resin binder. The agency also notes that curves and junctions require significantly higher levels of friction than straight roads, especially in rainy weather.Washington State tried it in Everett, in Snohomish County. In June 2015, engineers applied a covering of resin and bauxite to the eastbound State Route 526 ramp to southbound Interstate 5. In the five years before treatment, the ramp averaged 13.8 wet surface crashes a year. In the year after, it recorded one, according to a 2017 Washington State Department of Transportation analysis. To understand those results, it helps to know what was laid down on the road and how it grips.Bauxite meets resinCalcined bauxite is conventional bauxite ore that has been heated to 1,000-1,200 degrees Celsius. The heating drives off moisture and increases the alumina concentration, leaving a highly durable aggregate that remains rough under traffic. Crews spread a polymer resin binder over the pavement, then drop the bauxite chips onto it before it sets, locking each chip in place. According to the Federal Highway Administration, the bond is strong enough to resist aggressive cornering, harsh braking and even snowploughs.Bauxite is not the only stone engineers have tried. In a 2015 study, the National Center for Asphalt Technology at Auburn University tested granite, flint, basalt, silica sand, steel slag, emery and taconite against calcined bauxite, which provided the best friction performance. Skid-trailer readings showed bauxite's friction number dropping from 70 to 63, against 54 to 40 for granite and 54 to 43 for flint. Engineers see it as a spot fix for places where wet skids keep happening, largely because the layer is thin and sits on top of the old asphalt instead of replacing it. The results at those spots are the more telling part.Two ramps, big dropsThat same month, WSDOT also treated an Eastgate on-ramp, from 148th Avenue SE to westbound Interstate 90. Friction readings at both locations rose from the upper 30s to the low to mid 70s. The analysis compared a five-year average with the first year after installation, from July 2015 to June 2016. On the State Route 526 ramp, collisions on wet surfaces dropped from an average of 13.8 a year to one, a 93% decrease. All crashes there, wet and dry, dropped from 17.6 to seven. The Eastgate ramp did even better on wet roadways, with wet surface crashes falling from 23.2 a year to one.The spread between those numbers is telling. A comparable ramp in Vancouver, Washington, treated with a two-part epoxy product called Tyregrip, saw wet-weather run-off-the-road crashes fall from 24 to five over the five years after treatment, a decline of 79 per cent, while all other crashes fell by only 10 per cent. Injuries from crashes dropped from seven to one. Not all crashes are caused by skids on the surface.There’s a warning on the same ramp in Vancouver too. The first application in 2010 raised friction just a little, but the provider reapplied it in May 2011, and measurements jumped to about 77. Later the overlay started to fracture and peel, and by the end of the research in May 2016, huge chunks had come away. WSDOT couldn’t narrow down the source, but it suggested that dampness in the underlying asphalt or the tremendous load on the surface from rotating tyres could be the cause. Friction stayed in the 70s throughout, and the crash benefit held.What the wider evidence saysFlorida started employing the surfaces in 2006, and a 2016 analysis of 47 installations found an average 32% reduction in total crashes and a 75% reduction in rainy weather crashes. It also found that 22% of the systems were in poor or failed condition, with loss of aggregate being the most common concern.The other thing is the cost. The Vancouver ramp cost $43,800 for 1,200 square yards in 2010, roughly $36.50 a square yard, according to WSDOT's Tyregrip evaluation. Florida’s overall expenses were between $36 and $113. That is pricey by regular resurfacing standards, but a Texas study cited by WSDOT suggested that avoiding even one fatal crash can return almost 100 times the initial investment. A 2020 FHWA study reached a similar conclusion, finding significant crash reductions from high-friction surface treatments at curves and ramps, particularly for wet-weather crashes.The lessons for road agencies are rather clear. This solution works well for short segments where wet skids tend to group together, such as a sudden ramp or bend, not long straight highways. The pavement below must be solid and clean, as this area is where several of the failures started. And no surface will prevent every crash. Still, it's tough to argue with a decline from roughly 14 rainy weather collisions a year to one, and that explains why more states keep reaching for resin and bauxite.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2020, Texas boy Orion Jean used a $500 speech-contest prize to launch a kindness drive; it grew from more than 600 toys to 100,000 meals and 500,000 books, and he is now pursuing one million acts of kindness
articles.summary: Orion Jean, a Texas teenager, turned a $500 speech contest prize into a massive kindness initiative, distributing over 500,000 books, 100,000 meals, and aiming for one million acts of kindness. Discover his inspiring journey and the impact of Race to Kindness.
articles.body: A $500 prize from a school speech contest led a Texas teenager to launch a toy drive for children at a local hospitalOrion Jean,15, is the founder of Race to Kindness, a youth-led initiative that encourages people to identify needs around them and respond through practical acts of service. He was named TIME’s 2021 Kid of the Year and has gone on to become an author and public speaker.The idea began in 2020, when Jean took part in a national kindness speech contest. In his speech, he argued that kindness was something anyone could practise and that people could choose to act rather than wait for someone else to make a difference.Jean told Reading Is Fundamental (RIF), a non-profit children's literacy organization in the United States, that winning the contest became the “catalyst” for something much bigger. He used the $500 prize as seed money for his first project, Race to 500 Toys.With help from his community, Jean collected more than 600 toys for a local hospital, according to his account of the initiative.From toys to mealsThe first campaign was followed by a much larger effort to address food insecurity.Jean launched the Race to 100,000 Meals with the support of volunteers, corporate donors and a local nonprofit organisation. The campaign collected more than 100,000 meals for families facing food insecurity in Texas, he said in an interview with RIF.The scale of the projects changed, but Jean said the basic idea remained the same: identify a problem and find people willing to help address it.That approach eventually led him to focus on children's access to books.Jean has described reading as a major influence on how he understands other people and the world around him. In the interview, he said books allow him to experience different cultures and perspectives and “walk in someone else’s shoes”.His next campaign, Race to 500,000 Books, eventually exceeded its target. As per RIF, the initiative resulted in more than half a million books being donated to school districts, nonprofits and children through Race to Kindness free book fairs held across the US.Jean has said he wants children to have the same access to books that he had growing up.Why books became the next targetFor Jean, the book campaign was not simply about putting more books into children's hands. He connected access to reading with a child's ability to learn, explore different perspectives and develop a broader understanding of the world.Jean said his own interest in reading helped shape many of his experiences. He argued that every child should have access to books.The campaign also involved RIF, Jean later partnered with the organisation for reading events, including a nationwide Read Across America Day programme.His work with books has become one of the defining parts of Race to Kindness. The organisation says its broader efforts have included more than 500,000 books, more than 100,000 meals and hundreds of toys distributed to children in hospitals and underserved communities.Jean has written A Kids Book About Leadership and Race to Kindness, using books to extend the message behind his community work.He has also said that his long-term interests include storytelling through writing or directing, although he has not settled on a specific career path.The next target for Race to Kindness is significantly larger than the campaigns that came before it: one million acts of kindness.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'Unusual request': EC explains why it could not meet Rahul Gandhi-led opposition MPs
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Amid the onging row with opposition parties over SIR, the Election Commission of India on Tuesday said that no political party had formally
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Amid the onging row with opposition parties over SIR, the Election Commission of India on Tuesday said that no political party had formally sought an appointment to meet."Earlier today, during the march of certain political parties towards the Election Commission, it was learnt through the media that some Members of Parliament wished to meet the Commission along with their delegation. With regard to today's developments, it is clarified that, till 4.00 PM today, no political party, through its representatives, had sought an appointment for a meeting with the Election Commission," said the EC in a statement.The EC added that it found out through Delhi Police that "a delegation of MPs, led by the Hon'ble leader of the opposition, Shri Rahul Gandhi, wished to meet the Commission and submit a memorandum."Further clarifying the rules and justifying itself, the EC cited procedures laid down for meetings with political parties. "All political parties had been informed of the same and they follow this procedure. Whenever a delegation of a political party, or a joint delegation of several parties, wishes to meet the Commission, it seeks an appointment through its duly Authorised Representative. The meeting is thereafter held at a time mutually agreed upon by both sides," it said.The EC further claimed that after 4 PM, while it was considering the proposed meeting, the Delhi Police informed it that the delegation comprised 240 MPs and that they wanted to meet at the Parliament House Annexe. The Commission termed the request “unusual” and said it could not be accepted because, under ECI protocol, meetings with political parties are held only at the Commission’s premises.The poll panel said it then offered to send its senior-most officer on duty to the Parliament House Annexe to receive the MPs’ memorandum. The EC described this as “an unprecedented step”, but said the offer was also declined by the MPs.The Commission said it respected “the parliamentary and democratic processes of the country”, while stressing that its own protocols and conventions were also important. It reiterated that political parties can request meetings with the EC at any time, after which the Commission schedules a date and time depending on its availability.This came as INDIA bloc leaders staged a massive march from Parliament towards the Election Commission headquarters, demanding a meeting with the poll panel over their allegations of “vote chori” and seeking the removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar. Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra joined the sit-in near Akashvani Bhavan, but police later cleared the protest site and detained several opposition MPs.Read more: Rahul and Priyanka removed from protest site after high drama - watchGet the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Lithuania ready to cover cost if US establishes military base; parliament votes to host foreign arms
articles.summary: Lithuanian Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevicius on Tuesday said the country would cover the cost if the US decides to establish a military base.
articles.body: Lithuanian Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevicius on Tuesday said the country would cover the cost if the US decides to establish a military base."Our partners only need to make the political ⁠decision to permanently station troops, and Lithuania is ready to cover the costs involved", Sinkevicius said.The Lithuanian PM had previously invited the Americans to establish a permanent presence in the country. Since 2019, Lithuania has hosted an armoured US battalion of almost 1,000 troops, which are deployed every few months on a rotational basis.On Monday, the US President Donald Trump said he would consider Lithuania's request."They are friends ⁠of mine, they are great people, so we will certainly look at it", he said.The PM’s remarks arrive on the day Lithuania's parliament voted, in a first of the two ballots, in favour of removing the constitutional ban on hosting nuclear arms on its territory.If passed by a two-thirds majority, it will remove the prohibitions set after the Nato member broke away from the Soviet Union, more than three decades ago.On Tuesday, Russia warned that Lithuania’s decision to host nuclear arms could lead to new escalations in the region.Asked by reporters how Russia viewed the proposal, as well as another development, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said moving US military infrastructure closer to Russia's borders can only be seen as a step toward greater tensions."If the military infrastructure of what is, in effect, Nato's leading country (the US) is moving closer to our borders, then, of course, this cannot be perceived as anything other than a step towards escalating tensions", Peskov said.Peskov said the same applied to the deployment of nuclear weapons on the territory of a neighbouring state."Neither of these developments will contribute to stability and predictability on the European continent; on the contrary, they will, much to our regret, mark yet another significant escalation of tensions," he added.You use AI every day. articles.title: California screamin’: Trump says Iran taking out LA and San Diego would be 'small price to pay'
articles.summary: TOI correspondent from Washington: MAGA boss Donald Trump has never been particularly sentimental about California, a state that has rejected him by 20 to
articles.body: TOI correspondent from Washington: MAGA boss Donald Trump has never been particularly sentimental about California, a state that has rejected him by 20 to 30 points in the last three presidential elections. But suggesting that Iran could “take out” Los Angeles or San Diego -- and calling their destruction “a very small price to pay” -- carried the president’s long-running feud with the Golden State into distinctly darker territory.At a rally in Grand Island, Nebraska, on Monday night, Trump was explaining away the economic pain caused by his war on Iran when his verbal GPS appeared to lose the signal. “With the war, it’s just artificial. It’s a little bit high,” Trump said, apparently referring to prices. Then came the sentence that jolted American politics: “It’s a small price to pay for keeping the world safe, keeping our country safe. They can take out a city. Let ’em take out Los Angeles. Let ’em take out San Diego.” The crowd, mostly Trump faithful, cheered.For the liberal-left phalanx, the comment was less about Iran than another Trump strike against California, a Democratic fortress. California Governor Gavin Newsom called Trump “deranged and dangerous.” Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass said the president’s job was to protect Americans, not encourage attacks on them. San Diego Mayor Todd Gloria snapped, “San Diego is not collateral damage. We are not expendable.”Ironically, San Diego is not just an American entrepot with golden beaches and lovely weather. It is home to one of Trump favored constituencies -- the American military. The city is a base to the Pacific Fleet, and includes major Navy and Marine installations, submarines, and aircraft carriers. An attack on San Diego would not simply ruin someone's weekend plans in La Jolla; it would hit a major component of American military power.“San Diego is a proud military town, home to 115,000 courageous active duty service members and their families. Military service is at the root of our community and culture. This month we await the return home of the sailors and marines still stranded on the USS Lincoln for months thanks to Donald Trump’s reckless war in Iran,” raged Congressman Scott Peters, a San Diego Democrat, asserting that “America knows San Diego is not a “small price to pay” for his inability to resolve it.”The White House rapid-response team promptly went into linguistic damage control. “No, he didn't, you buffoons,” it pushed back, arguing that Trump was not inviting Iran to attack California, but explaining why the US must prevent Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons capable of attacking American cities. That defense has one problem: the footage and the transcript: “Let ’em take out Los Angeles. Let ’em take out San Diego,” before declaring the loss “a very small price to pay.”This is where Trump's unique oratorical skill, which some have compared to that of a third-grader, becomes politically hazardous. His defenders have to routinely perform interpretive gymnastics worthy of a trapeze artist because the president's trademark rambling leaves them explaining what he must have meant -- while opponents quote what he actually said.The timing of the latest flub could hardly be worse for Republicans. Four weeks before the midterm elections on November 3, a Reuters/Ipsos poll released Monday put Trump's approval at just 32%, while Democrats led Republicans nationally among registered voters 44% to 37%. Several surveys shows Democrat candidates for Senate and governorships leading in such unlikely red states as Texas and Kansas.Even Republicans are now showing signs of Trump fatigue. MAGA rallies of yore were political oxygen for Trump: enormous crowds, roaring chants, the candidate basking in adulation. Lately, reports describe smaller crowds, visible empty sections and supporters leaving before Trump finishes. Trump, though, insists the enthusiasm is “hotter than ever” -- presumably not as hot as Californians under the collar this week.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: In 2024, researchers turned discarded plastic bottles and stone into pothole-repair surfacing; strength, stiffness and durability exceeded typical road-infrastructure requirements
articles.summary: Researchers at the University of Dodoma developed a new pothole repair material using melted PET plastic bottles combined with sand and gravel, surpassing conventional asphalt performance.
articles.body: Potholes are a familiar problem for road users, damaging vehicles, slowing traffic and creating hazards for cyclists and pedestrians. Repairing them usually involves asphalt-based mixtures, but these materials can be expensive, and poorly executed patches may deteriorate under repeated traffic loads and exposure to water. Researchers have been exploring whether discarded plastic can offer an alternative, tackling road maintenance and plastic waste at the same time.In December 2024, a study published in Frontiers in Engineering and Built Environment investigated a different approach: melting waste plastic bottles and combining the material with sand and crushed stone to produce a surface for pothole repairs. The research, conducted at the University of Dodoma in Tanzania, found that the best-performing mixture exceeded conventional benchmarks in several mechanical tests.Turning plastic waste into a road-repair materialThe research addressed two related problems: plastic pollution and road-maintenance costs. PET (polyethene terephthalate) is widely used in beverage packaging and discarded after use. Finding a use for this type of plastic could help divert some of it from disposal while reducing dependence on conventional construction materials. To experiment, the scientists collected used PET bottles from the University of Dodoma campus. The bottles were washed, cut into pieces measuring 10–20 mm, and dried in the sun for 24 hours. The plastic was then heated to 280°C before being mixed with sand and gravel in different proportions. The optimum mixture was later identified as 30% PET, 30% sand and 40% gravel by weight.Mixes were formed with varying percentages of PET, sand, and gravel to find out which one gave better mechanical results. This included mixes made entirely of PET as well as mixes with varying amounts of plastic and aggregate. The scientists created samples out of these materials and analysed them in laboratories. This was done with the intention of coming up with a formulation that can give the stability and stiffness required for pothole repair.The best-performing mixtureThe best-performing mixture contained 30% PET plastic, 30% sand and 40% gravel by weight. It was observed that the equilibrium ratio between the plastic binding agent and mineral aggregate components is crucial; an excess of plastic would make the mixture less strong. The right balance of sand and gravel made the mixture stronger and denser. Three factors were considered in analysing the material's behaviour.First was the Marshall Stability, which reflects resistance to deformation. The optimum mixture scored 59.78 kilonewtons (kN), compared with the usual 7–15 kN for common asphalt mixtures. The second test was the indirect tensile strength test, which evaluates a material’s resistance to tensile stress and cracking. This formulation had a tensile strength of 5,909 kilopascals (kPa). Third, the stiffness modulus was used to evaluate how the material responds to applied forces. In this test, they obtained a result of 36,145 megapascals (MPa). Based on these findings, the material met the mechanical requirements set by the researchers.From laboratory success to real-world roadsThese results suggest a way to use waste bottles as a building material while reducing reliance on traditional road-repair materials. Using locally available sand and gravel may also help in areas with tight road-maintenance budgets and abundant plastic waste. There are some issues that have not yet been clarified. Field tests need to be performed to determine the behaviour of the composite in a real-world setting in the presence of traffic, changing temperatures, and moisture.The energy required for melting should also be considered. Heating PET to 280 degrees Celsius takes energy and requires proper safety controls. Any assessment of the approach's environmental benefits would need to consider processing energy, possible emissions, worker safety, and how the material changes over time. Cost should also be considered. Even though the bottles are not costly, gathering, cleaning, cutting, and melting them does take some effort. A comparison with traditional patching should include these costs, along with installation and maintenance.For now, the study is seen as a promising laboratory result rather than a direct substitute for asphalt. Its primary value is to show that used plastic bottles may act as a binding agent in a sand-and-gravel repair mix without bitumen or cement. If further field tests confirm its strength and reliability, it could become another tool for pothole repair and a useful application for waste plastic bottles. It remains to be seen whether the product will work as reliably in the field as it does in the lab.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Man who died after Glasgow city centre attack named by police
articles.summary: Daniel Colrain died in hospital after being assaulted in Royal Exchange Square in the early hours of Sunday.
articles.body:
A 21-year-old man who died after being attacked in Glasgow city centre has been named by police.

Daniel Colrain was found with serious injuries in Royal Exchange Square at about 03:05 on Sunday. He died in hospital the following day.

A 19-year-old man has been arrested in connection with the disturbance and released pending further inquiries.

Another man, aged 21, was also assaulted and suffered minor injuries. A 20-year-old man has been charged in connection with this and is due to appear before Glasgow Sheriff Court at a later date.

A post-mortem examination took place earlier.

Police Scotland have appealed for information about the attack and have set up a dedicated portal where information can be submitted anonymously.

Daniel's family are being supported by specialist officers.

Det Insp Jonny MacKinnon, of Greater Glasgow CID, said: "Our thoughts remain with Daniel's family and friends at what is an extremely difficult time for them.

"I would like to reiterate that no arrests have been made in connection with the death at this time and extensive inquiries remain ongoing to establish the full circumstances.

"It is vital we get answers for Daniel's family."

Ch Insp Stephen McManus added: "We understand this incident will be concerning for the community but please be assured specialist officers are carrying out extensive inquiries.

"Increased patrols will be carried out in the area and anyone with any concerns, or information, can approach these officers."

articles.title: EU ready to send observers for first Palestinian parliamentary vote in nearly two decades
articles.summary: The European Union on Tuesday said it was ready to deploy election observers for the Palestinian legislative elections scheduled for November.
articles.body: The European Union on Tuesday said it was ready to deploy election observers for the Palestinian legislative elections scheduled for November.EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas made the announcement on X after speaking with Palestinian vice president Hussein Al-Sheikh."Palestinians have the right to choose their representatives in elections that are credible, inclusive and transparent," she wrote. On X.Kallas added that after nearly 20 years without a parliamentary vote, the elections would offer a long-overdue opportunity to renew the legitimacy of Palestinian institutions.Palestinian president Mahmoud Abbas has set November 28 as the date for the legislative polls. If they go ahead, it will be the first such vote in two decades.Holding elections is among the reforms demanded by the international community, including the European Union, which provides financial support to the Ramallah-based Palestinian Authority. AFP reported.The Palestinian territories last held legislative elections in 2006, when Hamas defeated Abbas's Fatah party, which had previously dominated Palestinian politics. Since then, the Palestinian Legislative Council, the parliament of Abbas's Palestinian Authority, has not met since 2007.Palestinians did return to the polls in April, when they elected municipal council heads in the occupied West Bank. That was the first vote since the Gaza war broke out in October 2023.The legislative elections, however, face major logistical challenges stemming from Israeli measures in the Gaza Strip, East Jerusalem and the West Bank, all of which Israel has occupied since 1967.You use AI every day. articles.summary: Khloe Thompson, a California teenager, launched Khloe Kares, a nonprofit that has distributed over 5,000 handmade care bags filled with essentials for women experiencing homelessness. Discover her inspiring journey and impact in the community.
articles.body: A California teenager who once made bags with her great-grandmother now runs a nonprofit that has distributed more than 5,000 handmade care bags to women experiencing homelessness.Khloe Thompson started the project after encountering a woman living on the street while walking to school with her mother. At the time, Thompson was 9 and wanted to understand why people in her community were living without homes.She later decided to use the sewing skills she had developed with her great-grandmother to make something useful for women in need.From homemade bags to a nonprofitThompson and her great-grandmother began making shoulder and tote bags together several days a week. Thompson suggested filling the bags with basic items and giving them to women living in tents and shelters.Her great-grandmother agreed to pay for the supplies needed for the first batch. After the initial distributions, the family looked for ways to continue the project.In 2015, Thompson founded “Khloe Kares” as a nonprofit organisationThe organisation's main project is the Kare Bag, a handmade tote containing everyday personal-care supplies. According to Khloe Kares, more than 5,000 of the bags have been distributed to women experiencing homelessness.The bags include necessities such as toothbrushes, toothpaste, soap, lotion, feminine hygiene products, socks and underwear. Some also contain a small surprise gift.Community groups help expand the effortKhloe Kares has relied on partnerships to increase the number of people it can reach. Local businesses, churches and nonprofit organisations have helped collect supplies and organise distribution events.During Kare Bag events, partner groups gather the products needed to fill the bags, while Khloe Kares provides the handmade totes and helps with distribution.The organisation says its goal is not only to provide immediate necessities but also to raise awareness about homelessness and support women as they work towards more stable housing.Thompson's work has since moved beyond the care bags. She has also taken part in projects aimed at supporting children and young people, including efforts in Ghana involving water pumps and bathroom facilities at schools.She has also worked with her mother on workshops for young people covering topics such as business planning, public speaking, confidence and goal-setting.RecognitionIn 2019, she helped launch #GivingTuesdayKids in partnership with the global GivingTuesday movement. The initiative encouraged young people to organise volunteer projects and acts of service based on causes they cared about.Her work has also received recognition. Thompson was among the recipients of the 2019 George H.W. Bush Points of Light Awards, which recognise people for community service.The award recognised her work with Khloe Kares and other youth-focused initiatives. Points of Light President and CEO Natalye Paquin said Thompson represented a generation of young people taking an active role in shaping their communities.Thompson has continued to emphasise that young people do not have to wait until they are older to contribute.You use AI every day. articles.title: 13 Navy personnel under scanner in Pakistan-linked espionage probe
articles.summary: Andhra Pradesh CI launches Operation Firewall-2026 in Pak-linked espionage probe; 18 under scanner including 13 Navy staff; 2 arrested for leaking defence intel.
articles.body: VIJAYAWADA: A suspected Pakistan-linked espionage network has triggered a major counter-intelligence operation across Andhra Pradesh and other parts of the country, with 18 people under the scanner, including 13 suspected Navy personnel.The state counter-intelligence (CI) wing has launched ‘Operation Firewall-2026’, deploying 12 teams to conduct simultaneous searches across 10 states and union territories, including Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Maharashtra and Karnataka. The operation is focused on suspected links between the suspected individuals and Pakistan intelligence operatives (PIOs), particularly through encrypted communication platforms.Investigators are probing the alleged targeting of sensitive information related to Indian Navy and defence establishments in Visakhapatnam, a strategically important naval hub on India’s eastern coast. Officials suspect that confidential information may have been collected and shared with Pakistan-linked operatives. Electronic devices were reportedly seized from several suspects during the searches. Preliminary evidence has emerged against at least two of the 18 suspects, officials said.In Visakhapatnam, counter-intelligence unit sleuths arrested Annam Sai Varaprasad, a civilian contract driver working with the Navy, for allegedly passing sensitive information about defence establishments to a Pakistan-linked operative. Investigators are examining whether he received money in exchange for the information. Varaprasad was produced before a court and remanded in judicial custody until Oct 14. He was subsequently lodged in Visakhapatnam district jail.In a related incident, a 31-year-old Navy sailor, identified as Pradeep Mukherjee, was arrested from Coimbatore on Saturday. Mukherjee, who joined the Indian Navy in 2014 and was attending a training course in Coimbatore when he was arrested, is accused of leaking classified maritime intelligence to Pakistan-linked operatives after reportedly falling into a honeytrap.He was arrested following a months-long joint operation by the counter-intelligence units of AP and Tamil Nadu police. Mukherjee was brought from Coimbatore on a transit warrant and remanded in judicial custody till Oct 14. He is currently lodged in Vijayawada district jail.The probe against the remaining 16 suspects is continuing. articles.title: Gujarat: Lover forced into sex act with woman in public as ‘punishment’ for affair
articles.summary: Surendranagar “purification ritual” case: 9 arrested after woman and partner were assaulted, forced into sex acts and humiliation; videos went viral online.
articles.body: RAJKOT: In a horrifying case of vigilante brutality, a man was allegedly forced to perform sexual acts with a married woman with whom he was in a relationship and made to drink her urine as “punishment” in public glare as a so-called “purification ritual” in Surendranagar.The woman and her partner were allegedly subjected to the ordeal by her husband and his relatives on Oct 4. The accused also recorded the acts on mobile phones and circulated the videos on social media.Police traced the woman after coming across the viral videos and arrested nine people, including her husband and his relatives.According to the complaint, the woman was married to a man in Vapi. She had left her husband and moved to Chotila, where she lived with her partner for around three months. Her family later traced her, brought her back to Vapi and allegedly confined her in a house. She eventually escaped and returned to Chotila five days ago.When her husband learnt that she was back with her partner, he allegedly alerted his relatives, who traced the couple, brought them to a house in Surendranagar and subjected them to the alleged “purification ritual”.Talking to TOI, Surendranagar DSP Premsukh Delu said police learnt about the incident after a community leader alerted them and videos of the assault surfaced on social media.“I received a call from a community leader regarding a woman who had been brutalised. We also came across several videos. Several police teams were deployed to trace the woman,” Delu said.Police teams searched houses in the area and found the woman at one of them. “She started crying on seeing the police. We matched her face with the woman in the video and brought her to the police station. She narrated her ordeal after counselling,” Delu said.According to the complaint, the accused brought the couple to Surendranagar, claiming they were going to perform a “purification ritual”. They allegedly beat them with wooden sticks and thrashed them. The man was then tied to a tree with a rope, while the woman was confined to a room.The accused allegedly later forced the man to perform sexual acts with the woman in a verandah and subjected both to further humiliation. The man was also allegedly forced to drink the woman’s urine. The entire ordeal was recorded on a mobile phone and the videos circulated on social media, police said.RM Sangada, inspector, A-Division police station, said police are also investigating who recorded the videos and circulated them on social media.The accused have been booked under various sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, including Sections 70(1) (sexual intercourse by deceitful means), 115(2) (voluntarily causing hurt), 127(3) (wrongful confinement), 142 (wrongfully concealing or keeping a kidnapped/abducted person) and 3(5) (acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention), as well as provisions of the IT Act.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Rajkot | Silver Rate in Rajkot | Bank Holidays in Rajkot | Public Holidays in Rajkot | Rajkot AQI | Weather in Rajkot | Petrol Price in Rajkot | Diesel Price in Rajkot | CNG Price in Rajkot | LPG Price in RajkotStay updated with the latest Rajkot news. articles.title: A manure-lagoon overflow at a Maryland dairy farm killed nearly 11,000 fish across 25 species, state officials say; the farm already faces a pollution lawsuit and a civil-contempt request over alleged violations
articles.summary: An overflow from a manure lagoon at Kilby Farms in Cecil County, Maryland, has killed nearly 11,000 fish across 25 species in Basin Run, according to the
articles.body: An overflow from a manure lagoon at Kilby Farms in Cecil County, Maryland, has killed nearly 11,000 fish across 25 species in Basin Run, according to the Maryland Department of the Environment. The incident, which came to light in early October 2026, marks a far larger fish kill than a similar event at the same farm in 2025. State officials say the discharge occurred as the dairy already faces a lawsuit and a civil-contempt request over alleged repeated violations of a 2025 settlement aimed at stopping pollution in the waterway, as per reports.A creek choked with dead fishBasin Run is a small but ecologically important stream in northeast Maryland. It flows west through Cecil County before emptying into the Susquehanna River and, ultimately, the Chesapeake Bay. The creek is known locally for its population of wild trout and has long been a favourite spot for fishing and outdoor recreation.This week, however, the stream was lined with dead fish for more than four miles, from Kilby Farms downstream to Octoraro Creek. Chris Thomas, a neighbour who grew up on Basin Run and still lives alongside it, described the scene as worse than anything he had seen before, as per The Banner. He told reporters that foamy water and dead fish, including tiny minnows, trout and eels, floated in the stream, with a stench lingering over the area.The Maryland Department of the Environment estimates that nearly 11,000 fish died across 25 species. Preliminary findings point to an overflow at a Kilby Farms manure lagoon as the cause. The agency described the incident as unacceptable and said it was taking the issue very seriously, noting that it had already obtained a preliminary injunction barring the facility from discharging pollution into the waterway.A farm already under legal pressureThe fish kill comes as Kilby Farms faces a lawsuit from the Maryland Department of the Environment over alleged repeated discharges of manure and other pollutants into Basin Run. The state sued the dairy and an associated real estate company this year over failures to comply with a 2025 settlement that was meant to end discharges of foul liquid into the creek, as per reports.Under Maryland law, large-animal operations such as dairy farms require approvals to regulate and prevent discharges. Despite housing hundreds of cows, Kilby Farms does not have permit coverage, according to state officials. Testing by Maryland regulators has found depleted water quality and significantly less life in Basin Run downstream from the farm, reinforcing concerns about the impact of ongoing pollution.The agency has now asked a judge to hold the dairy in civil contempt over continued violations. A hearing on that motion is scheduled for October 13 in a Cecil County courtroom. The state says it is seeking to enforce the preliminary injunction and ensure that the facility stops discharging pollution into the waterway, as per reports.Neighbours react to another disasterThe Banner further reported that for neighbours downstream from Kilby Farms, the latest fish kill is the latest chapter in a long-running environmental struggle. Larry McCracken Jr., who has watched pollution in Basin Run for years, said he is encouraged to see others worried about the problem but hopes solutions do not come at the cost of individual livelihoods. He believes many issues on the property date back decades and predate the current operator.Chris Thomas, who once described a Basin Run fish kill from a year ago as the worst environmental thing he had ever seen, said this week’s incident surpassed even that, reported The Banner. He donned waders to assess the stream with MDE inspectors and said the damage extended more than four miles downstream. His frustration echoes that of other residents who have taken to social media to express anger over the repeated incidents.Video posted in a new Protect Basin Run Facebook group shows foamy water flowing through the creek, with comments from residents asking when the dumping of cow manure will stop. The online reaction reflects a growing sense of urgency among community members who feel that years of pollution have gone unchecked.The farm’s response and disputed claimsNeither the owner of the dairy operation, Pennsylvania farmer Ben Flahart, nor his attorney responded to phone calls or text messages about the latest fish kill, The Banner reported. Attorney Anthony Gorski has argued that many issues on the Kilby Farms property date back decades but have attracted scrutiny only since Flahart took over in 2017. He has also said he has not seen proof that the incidents in Basin Run were caused by Kilby Farms, the report further suggested.Gorski has taken issue with the state’s testing methods, saying regulators failed to account for pollution that flows through the farm and into Basin Run from a different tributary. He said his own testing shows high bacteria levels upstream from Kilby, suggesting that not all of the contamination can be attributed to the dairy. Flahart has told reporters he believes he has been targeted by a liberal environmental department under Democratic Governor Wes Moore.The farmer paid a $50,000 penalty under the 2025 settlement with MDE and said he has spent millions more on improved operations and environmental compliance. He recently removed a drainage pond that had been blamed for much of the pollution. Despite those efforts, state officials say violations have continued, leading to the current contempt request.What happens nextThe October 13 hearing will focus on whether Kilby Farms should be held in civil contempt for alleged continued violations of the 2025 settlement and the preliminary injunction. If the judge finds the dairy in contempt, additional penalties or restrictions could follow. The outcome will shape how aggressively the state can enforce its orders and what further measures might be required to protect Basin Run.In the meantime, the fish kill has renewed calls for stronger oversight of large-animal operations and better protection for streams that feed into the Chesapeake Bay. For neighbours like Thomas and McCracken, the issue is personal. They have watched the creek they love suffer repeated blows and now hope that legal action will finally lead to lasting change.The Maryland Department of the Environment says it is taking the issue very seriously and will continue to pursue enforcement. How the case unfolds could set a precedent for how the state handles pollution from agricultural operations in sensitive watersheds. For Basin Run, the stakes are high, as the creek’s future depends on whether the discharges can be stopped and the ecosystem allowed to recover.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: British Indian peer Lord Ranger wins right to judicial review of CBE annulment
articles.summary: LONDON: British Indian Tory peer Lord Rami Ranger, aka Raminder Singh Ranger, has won a historic right to judicial review of the decision to strip him of
articles.body: LONDON: British Indian Tory peer Lord Rami Ranger, aka Raminder Singh Ranger, has won a historic right to judicial review of the decision to strip him of his CBE (Commander of the Order of the British Empire) in 2024 after he was accused of breaching the parliamentary code of conduct.Lord Ranger took the office of the UK PM to court in June over the decision by King Charles to revoke the honour bestowed on him by the late Queen Elizabeth II for services to business and community cohesion.King annulled the CBE on Oct 15, 2024, on the recommendation of then PM Keir Starmer, who took advice from the honours forfeiture committee after it deemed Ranger to have “brought the honours system into disrepute”.The UK govt tried to get the case thrown out, saying the decision to revoke an honour fell under prerogative powers that are non-justiciable before the courts as it is a discretionary decision.But on Tuesday, Justice Nathalie Lieven found that the decision to revoke an honour is a justiciable one as there is a procedure to follow set out in the honours forfeiture handbook.“The removal of an honour has very significant consequences to individuals in terms of public reputational damage. Judicial review provides an important means of protecting individuals from errors or abuse in the exercise of official authority and is a fundamental part of the adherence to the rule of law,” she said.Lord Ranger can now proceed to a full judicial review of the decision to strip him of his honour, which will be unprecedented in Britain. His lawyers will argue that the decision to revoke his CBE was disproportionate and an attack on free speech, and that the forfeiture committee failed to follow due process.You use AI every day. articles.title: In Rejinagar, police detain last time’s winner hours after by-election starts
articles.summary: Rejinagar bypoll hit by rigging claims and police interference; AJUP chief Humayun Kabir detained as opposition seeks repoll; EC seeks report.
articles.body: Rejinagar/Kolkata: The Rejinagar bypoll saw widespread allegations of police interference and rigging and detention of Aam Janata Unnayan Party (AJUP) chief Humayun Kabir, prompting the entire opposition to demand a fresh election.When Kabir, father of AJUP candidate Golam Nabi Azad, visited a party office 700 metres from a polling station, Rejinagar IC Anjan Barman ordered him to head home. “Why should I go? How can you push me out of here?” Kabir shouted. Video footage showed police grabbing him by the shirt and bundling him into a vehicle and taken to Rejinagar police station.Released after 12 hours in detention, he told reporters late on Tuesday, “I will recommend a Padma Shri for the Murshidabad SP and a Bharat Ratna for EC.” Earlier in the day, Kabir alleged that police had forced his party’s agents out of booths and confiscated voter slips.Police said Kabir was neither a candidate nor an authorised agent of any candidate, and accused him of provoking unrest. Murshidabad SP Sachin Makkar backed the police action, while Election Commission (EC) sought a report of the incident.CM Suvendu Adhikari said: “Everyone should abide by the law. What he did was very harmful for democracy. If Suvendu Adhikari leaves this booth and goes to other booths, that, too, would be a violation. Suvendu Adhikari may be CM, but police can detain him if he does anything illegal.”The bypoll, which recorded an 80 per cent turnout, became necessary after Kabir chose to vacate Rejinagar and retain Nawda.The turnout touched 18% by 9 am, 56.4% by 1 pm and 69.2% by 3 pm. AJUP candidate Azad said, “Nobody could cast their vote. So there is no doubt than BJP is gong to win. There would have been a contest had there been a fair poll.”Hours after Kabir was whisked away by cops in the morning, Congress candidate Mohammad Abdullahil Kafi held a sit-in outside the police station, demanding a repoll. Former Congress MP Adhir Chowdhury led a protest in Berhampore. Congress lodged a complaint with the CEO’s office in Kolkata alleging large-scale rigging and demanding repoll.Mamata Trinamool candidate Rabiul Alam Chowdhury mentioned “booth capturing, rigging and the blocking of polling agents” in his complaint to EC. He also alleged that his party’s agents were driven out of over 200 booths and polling began before the scheduled time at many places.Mamata Trinamool spokesperson Kunal Ghosh said, “Votes were looted using police and govt machinery. BJP workers were given a free hand to loot votes.”Democratic Trinamool neta Akhruzzaman alleged: “They (BJP and police) were working hand-in-glove with each other. It was a rigged match, designed to help the BJP candidate.”Denying electoral malpractice, CM Adhikari said, “A police observer from Karnataka is here. A general observer has arrived from Tripura. I have also heard that another police observer came from Jharkhand. Which parties are in power in those states?”In front of one of the booths, BJP candidate Shankharavh Sarkar got involved in an altercation with central forces after he was ordered to move away for shaking hands with voters in the queue.Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya said, “You will be surprised by the Rejinagar result. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Cabinet on Tuesday adopted a resolution hailing the achievements of Narendra Modi in the last 25 years, first as chief minister of Gujarat and
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Cabinet on Tuesday adopted a resolution hailing the achievements of Narendra Modi in the last 25 years, first as chief minister of Gujarat and subsequently as PM.I&B minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said the resolution marks Modi's uninterrupted public service between Oct 7, 2001 and Oct 7, 2026. The resolution listed decisions taken by Modi which have touched the lives of common man and has given the country confidence. Vaishnaw said Modi's success and long service is a result of people's trust and faith in his style of governance and a vibrant example of the strength of Indian democracy.The resolution highlighted PM's tenure with a list of policy and political mandate he has got in Gujarat and at Centre. It mentioned initiatives from Modi's tenure as Gujarat CM that were adopted and extended at the national level. These included SWAGAT, the grievance-redressal system through which Modi interacted with citizens in Gujarat, and PRAGATI, Centre's platform for reviewing major projects and resolving implementation hurdles.It also cited Gujarat's Jyotigram scheme, which created separate agricultural electricity feeders, as an approach subsequently expanded nationally. The resolution linked Modi's experience of poverty with welfare initiatives, citing 60 crore Jan Dhan accounts, over 4 crore homes and 25 crore people moving out of poverty.It highlighted women's empowerment, saying nearly 3.5 crore women had become Lakhpati Didis, while Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam provided for women's reservation.PM-KISAN transfers exceeding Rs 4 lakh crore and PM-JANMAN for vulnerable tribal groups were also cited.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: BenDaDonnn vows legal action after arrest, claims ‘racial profiling’ and questions $7,000 bond
articles.summary: BenDaDonnn has spoken out after being arrested in College Station, Texas, following a confrontation with police outside The Spot after the Texas A&M vs.
articles.body: BenDaDonnn has spoken out after being arrested in College Station, Texas, following a confrontation with police outside The Spot after the Texas A&M vs. Arkansas football game. The streamer said he believes he was racially profiled and claimed he was wrongfully detained. He also said he plans to take legal action against the officers involved. Police, however, gave a different account of the incident, saying the group refused commands to clear the roadway. BenDaDonnn was charged with evading arrest or detention and released after posting a $7,000 bond. His security guard was also arrested.BenDaDonnn gives his side after College Station arrestBenDaDonnn, whose real name is Benjamin Beard, discussed the arrest during a livestream on October 5. He appeared on stream wearing prison-style clothes with a jail backdrop while explaining what happened.According to the College Station Police Department, officers were clearing people from the roadway outside The Spot when they encountered a group that “refused to comply” with their commands. Police said one person slapped an officer’s hand away when the officer tried to move him from the roadway.The department said another man, who later identified himself as Beard’s security guard, interfered when officers tried to detain the first suspect. Police said a less-lethal tool was then used on Beard as he attempted to get away. Beard was later charged with evading arrest or detention. His security guard, Kenny Carter, was charged with interference with public duties. Both men were released on bond.Beard gave a different version of the encounter. He said he believes race played a role in how the officer treated him.“What I do want to say is, I do believe that I was racially profiled, and I'm not here to make this into a crazy thing, but obviously I do think I was racially profiled,” Beard said. “[The officer] zoned in; he picked me, and he was like, 'Imma get yo' ***, brother.' We do got legal **** goin' on. We on it, 1000%. I was wrongfully accused; I was wrongfully detained.”Beard also questioned why he was being detained when the only charge he faced was evading arrest or detention.“The only thing I got accused of was evading. What am I being detained... What is you holding me for?.. I had been on the sidewalk since the first command... I just told you stop putting hands on people... So, what am I being detained for? Me talking back to you?”Why BenDaDonnn says his $7,000 bond made no senseBeard also compared his bond with Carter’s. According to police records reported by FOX 26 Houston, Beard’s bond was $7,000, while Carter’s was $4,000.Beard questioned why he had to pay more even though he said Carter was the person who made physical contact with an officer.“Me and Kenny was in that ****, locked down together. I don't know how the ****... My bond was like $7,000; Kenny's was $4,000. How?! Why I gotta pay more?.. I did realize I had my chain and my Richard Mille on; maybe that had something to do with it. But I ain't even do ****, brother... Why do I gotta pay more, and where is this money going?”Police have not said that Beard’s jewelry had anything to do with his bond amount.The College Station Police Department said the incident began while officers were trying to clear a busy roadway after the Texas A&M game. Police also said a large group later gathered around officers while Beard and Carter were waiting to be taken to jail, forcing officers to tell people to move back.Beard now says he plans to challenge what happened. As of October 6, no lawsuit had been filed, according to NDTV Sports. The criminal charge against him also remains an allegation and has not been decided in court.For now, the two sides are giving very different accounts. Police say Beard failed to follow commands and attempted to get away during the detention. Beard says he was already on the sidewalk, questioned the officers’ actions and believes he was targeted. The next step will depend on what happens with his case and any legal action he chooses to pursue.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
